archive_target.failure_domain: MinIO bound to 192.168.1.12, a real interface, so the archive path goes through the NIC and the routing table rather than the loopback shortcut. STILL ONE HOST: this does NOT demonstrate site loss. It removes one shortcut, nothing more.

node_loss.note: Recovery below reads the base backup and the OBJECT STORE only. Neither the crashed data directory nor any local archive directory exists at this point.

unverified: The object store runs on the SAME HOST as the database. This run proves the archive path works over the S3 protocol and that recovery needs nothing from the database's data directory -- the directory was deleted before recovery -- but it does NOT prove survival of a datacentre, region or availability zone. That needs a remote bucket and is stated as unverified for the same reason the kind/Helm row is.
No cross-region replication, object-lock or lifecycle policy is exercised. Those are bucket-side configuration and are documented in docs/DISASTER_RECOVERY.md, not measured here.

workload.crash_mode: pg_ctl stop -m immediate (no checkpoint, no final archive)

measured.notes: Continuous archive_mode=on with a real archive_command; recovery from base backup + archived WAL only. Segments were pushed to an S3-compatible object store over TCP, and the data directory was DELETED before recovery, so nothing here came from the database's own disk.
